parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the reverse-engineering rules, used only the bundled docs and CLI interaction, and targeted zk commands such as init, index, new, list, graph, edit, and tag list.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept final ownership while spawning a main probing child and nested helpers. One child expanded from probing into a full implementation owner, but there was no later parent-side integration of that implementation.
parallel.implementation: Two Python implementations emerged: the child wrote src/zk.py plus compile.sh and built an executable, while the parent later wrote a separate top-level zk.py plus compile.sh and patched that path.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact contained both src/zk.py and zk.py, but the final response described the parent's top-level zk.py and compile.sh as the delivered executable path.
parallel.verification: The parent ran representative smoke tests for version, help, notebook init, new, index, list, graph, and tag list, while the child also reported its own test set before being ignored.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent acknowledged unexhausted filter, sort, and TTY paths, and the official evaluator failed the solution despite the higher score.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room task and probed the public CLI, help, notebook behavior, FTS5 migration surface, formatting, filtering, graph, and tag behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, build, fixes, tests, and final delivery, with no child handoff or cross-agent result lifecycle.
serial.implementation: The serial solution was a Go codebase with go.mod, main.go, config.go, help.go, template.go, notebook.go, compile.sh, and a built executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The Go files and compile script formed one coherent final tree and the final response identified those files as the submitted implementation.
serial.verification: The serial actor built the executable and ran local smoke tests for help, notebook errors, init, list, tag list, graph, filters, and new dry-run or print-path flows.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final noted approximation gaps in interactive init and low-level warning or editor edge cases, and the official evaluator recorded many failures and errors.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail split: parallel failed at 573/1471 and serial failed at 229/1471. Parallel appears to have gained coverage from broader CLI probing and a Python implementation, but it also left a completed child implementation unjoined. Serial kept one-owner control and explored many behaviors, but its Go implementation still produced many evaluator failures and errors.
parallel_contributors: Child and helper probes captured substantial CLI surface and help/error behavior.
A completed child Python implementation existed but was not reconciled into the parent's delivered zk.py path.
The parent still ran representative smoke tests and closed with a higher, but failing, official score.
serial_contributors: The serial actor owned the whole Go implementation and build path without handoff risk.
It performed broad DB-seeded probing and local smoke tests but still closed with approximation gaps.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a Python script; serial delivered a Go binary.
Both final responses acknowledged unexhausted edge behavior, and the official evaluator exposed ordinary implementation incompleteness in both.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors only; no discordant pass/fail outcome is present
